quantifiers_route_objection: All locally convergent Gn and all fixed nonnegative integer k: chromatic root moments converge. Abért-Hubai v3 Theorem1.1 proves this under an absolute degree bound; selected proof and Theorem3.4 read. Without that convention, alternating empty graphs and K_m plus m^2 isolates gives first-moment limits 0 and 1/2, but this wording/domain issue earns no credit.

quantifiers_route_objection: Random d-regular graphs should converge locally-globally to weak closure of iid processes. Primary Q19 and nearby Q20 distinguish iid-action approximability. Local weak convergence alone does not prove local-global convergence or equality of coloring profiles.

title: Some Questions — Question 45
statement: Let an amenable group $\Gamma$ act ergodically and essentially faithfully on $X$. Is the groupoid cost of the action $1$? If $\Gamma$ is finitely presented, is this true for every infinite ergodic action?
quantifiers_route_objection: Every ergodic essentially faithful amenable action has groupoid cost1, plus every infinite ergodic action for finitely presented groups. Primary Q45 explicitly distinguishes essential faithfulness and infinitude. Cost of the orbit relation alone does not account for isotropy; do not import free-action theorem.
